best_in_this_half: base four-step; neither adapter provides a clear paired quality/calendar benefit
fourstep_vs_onestep: The base markedly improves skin/hair realism, especially dev06/09/12-trigger/13, and removes the dev07-trigger duplicate collar. This is an inference-step benefit already present without training. dev08/11/15 retain sculpted/etched texture and dev12-plain retains an eye defect; dev04 has poor cropped framing.
adaptation_effect: Step20 mostly ties base with one trigger-eye regression. Step100 more strongly smooths/chalks skin and introduces eye-detail regressions; no clear calendar wins in either prompt variant. One-step step100 dev04-trigger eye failure does not persist at four steps, but other failures remain.
gate_implication: Best trigger joint count in this half is base9/12, allowing at most21/24 even if every first-half case passes; below frozen22/24 criterion. Step20-trigger8/12 and step100-trigger6/12 are worse. No candidate in this half can establish the full development gate.
recommendation: Preserve all outcomes and report frozen pilot failure; do not open test seeds or extend training based on these images. Four-step base is a better research baseline, not a production-approved or trained-success result.
diversity: Twelve visually distinct case families remain in this half with an apparent age/hair/skin-tone range and no evident cross-case collapse. Not biometric identity verification or a full24-case family assessment.
limitations: Teacher memorization comparison not performed here.
No CUDA timing or public HTTP measurements performed.
Photographic appearance and calendar appeal are subjective visual judgements; full artifacts remain available.
